title: PRD: SaaS integrator onramp and fidelity presets
author: Priya Rao
body:
Overview:

This PRD describes a self-serve SaaS integrator onramp that accelerates product teams' adoption of Redwood by providing curated fidelity presets and a guided consumption simulator. The feature targets dev teams integrating Redwood API into a SaaS product who need quick, low-risk ways to estimate costs and select fidelity/latency tradeoffs appropriate for their use case.

Goals:
- Provide a minimal friction flow to pick a default fidelity preset (e.g., conversational-low-latency, conversational-cost-optimized, batch-embeddings-high-accuracy) and estimate 30/90/365-day costs given sample traffic patterns.
- Surface recommended runtime configuration (model variant, quantization profile, default batch size, KV cache policy) tied to the selected preset so customers can copy a working configuration into their Terraform/SDK onboarding.
- Collect lightweight telemetry during the onboarding simulation to improve future preset recommendations while preserving sensitive customer data.

Non-goals:
- This PRD does not replace full enterprise onboarding for Dedicated or Private deployments.
- It does not implement automatic billing commits or contract negotiation.

User personas:
1) Developer (early-stage SaaS startup): wants a fast path to sensible defaults and a cost estimate to justify usage in a demo.
2) Platform engineer (mid-market): needs predictable SLOs and guidance for model choices that satisfy latency SLAs.
3) Solutions engineer (sales-assisted onboarding): wants a reproducible profile to propose during initial calls.

High-level approach:
- Add a new "Onramp -> Fidelity Presets" wizard in the Console.
- Each preset bundles: suggested model variant, quantization profile, batching policy, KV cache hint, estimated tokens-per-request, and a 30/90/365-day cost simulation given user-supplied traffic curves.
- Expose an API endpoint for the simulator to accept synthetic traffic patterns (requests/sec distribution, avg tokens in/out) and return cost/latency/throughput projections.

Functional requirements (MUST):
1. Preset catalog: ship 6 curated presets for common SaaS workloads: transactional-chat, long-context-assistant, Q&A-embeddings, short-completion-notification, batched-embeddings, and low-cost-proxy. Each preset must include: model_variant, quant_profile, default_batch, kv_cache_policy, expected_tokens_in, expected_tokens_out, and an "estimated_latency_p50/p95" string.
2. Simulator API: POST /api/onramp/simulate accepts a JSON payload: {"preset_id","traffic_profile":{"rps":[],"burst_rps":[]},"avg_tokens_in","avg_tokens_out","duration_days"}. The response returns cost_estimate_usd (string), projected_p50_latency_ms, projected_p95_latency_ms, required_peak_gpu_slots.
3. Console UX: a stepper that collects minimal inputs (preset selection, expected monthly active users, avg interactions per user, sample payload size) and displays the simulation results with a clear call-to-action: Save preset, Export runtime config, Request SE assistance.
4. Export format: provide a downloadable YAML snippet and one-click copy to the SDK invocation and terraform snippet for Dedicated onboarding. Export must be stable across product versions for 12 months unless deprecated with clear migration notes.
5. Telemetry opt-in: telemetry is off by default; users can opt-in to send anonymized simulation telemetry (preset_id, non-sensitive traffic histogram, runtime_choice) for product improvement. Telemetry must strip any plain-text prompt or user content.

Non-functional requirements (SHOULD):
- The simulator must return results < 2s for typical inputs.
- Cost estimates should be within ±15% of actual hosted costs for steady-state workloads (documented assumptions).
- UX should be accessible (WCAG AA) and keyboard-navigable.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end flow validated by 3 internal use cases: (1) small SaaS with 5k MAU and 1 interaction/day, (2) mid-market with 50k MAU and 5 interactions/day, (3) enterprise POC with bursty traffic: able to select preset and export runtime config in < 5 minutes.
- A/B test shows >25% higher completion of onboarding-to-first-invocation compared to baseline wizard without presets.
- Telemetry opt-in rate across new signups ≥ 20% in first 60 days (opt-in shown only once).

Configuration matrix (sample table):

Preset             | Model Variant | Quant Profile | Default Batch | KV Cache | Expected tokens in/out | Typical P50 | Notes
------------------|----------------|---------------|---------------|----------|-----------------------|------------|------
transactional-chat| gptx-4-8b      | q8_0          | 8             | prefix   | 32 / 128              | 80ms       | low-latency
batch-embeddings  | emb-512        | f32           | 128           | none     | 1024 / 0              | 250ms      | throughput optimized
low-cost-proxy     | gptx-3-3b      | q4_0          | 1             | none     | 16 / 64               | 120ms      | cost-first

Telemetry and metrics to capture (anonymized):
- preset_id, runtime_choice, quant_profile, estimate_inputs: {avg_tokens_in,avg_tokens_out,expected_rps}
- simulator_result: {projected_cost_usd, projected_p50_ms, projected_p95_ms, required_peak_slots}
- event timestamps and correlation_id for troubleshooting

Security and privacy notes:
- Never capture prompt text, embeddings, or raw payloads in telemetry. Store only derived histograms (token-length buckets) and hashed preset IDs.
- If a customer toggles "share telemetry" then telemetry retention is 90 days by default and logged in audit trails.

Rollout plan and milestones:
1. 0–3 weeks: Backend simulator prototype, catalog data model, and minimal API. Internal smoke tests with synthetic traffic (owner: Eng Platform).
2. 3–6 weeks: Console wizard UX + export YAML/SDK snippets. SE playbook draft for recommended presets (owner: DX/PM).
3. 6–8 weeks: Public beta behind feature flag. Collect opt-in telemetry, run internal seeding with partner accounts.
4. 9–12 weeks: GA release, docs and tutorial, instrumentation for A/B measurement (owner: Growth/Product).

Operational considerations:
- Simulator will use cost-model parameters that must be kept in a versioned config (cost-per-GPU-hour, avg token compute cost). Include a /config/cost-model endpoint for ops to patch and a migration tag when parameters change.
- Add a smoke-test job in CI that validates the simulator's output format and latency SLA.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Should presets include a recommended fallback model variant for capacity-constrained periods? (tradeoff: complexity vs clearer guidance)
- What is the canonical governance process for adding new presets? Propose: Product creates a candidate, SE/Research validate against 3 workload profiles, then ship behind experimental flag.

Appendix: example simulator request/response (illustrative)

Request (POST /api/onramp/simulate):
{
  "preset_id": "transactional-chat",
  "traffic_profile": {"rps": [5, 20, 50], "burst_rps": [200]},
  "avg_tokens_in": 28,
  "avg_tokens_out": 120,
  "duration_days": 30
}

Response:
{
  "cost_estimate_usd": "1250.40",
  "projected_p50_latency_ms": "95",
  "projected_p95_latency_ms": "210",
  "required_peak_gpu_slots": "3"
}

Owners and next steps:
- Product: Priya Rao (PRD owner)
- Engineering: Ethan Moore (backend simulator), Lina Ortega (console UX)
- DX / Solutions: Sofia Alvarez (SE playbook)
- Metrics / Growth: Liam Patel (A/B measurement)

Next immediate actions (this week):
1. Align on the initial six presets and publish the specification for each (owner: Product).
2. Kick off prototype of the simulator API and cost model (owner: Eng Platform).
3. Draft the Console wizard wireframes and run a 1-hour design review with DX and Accessibility (owner: Eng DX).
